revelations.description: Lowered standards, returned keys, surrendered tokens, and delivered ledgers become obedience only when effective orders, inventories, subordinates, records, resources, and remedies change with them.

revelations.title: Government begins with the first order, not the final seal
revelations.description: A sealed Mandate is not yet a government: the settlement must specify the first field orders, transfers, pay and stores, public notices, correction routes, and interim petitions that begin before the autumn review.

revelations.title: The Emperor tests failure, not applause
revelations.description: The Emperor evaluates whether linked powers can obey, fail, be inspected, and be succeeded under Imperial authorship; clan approval matters as implementation evidence, not as a vote granting the Throne authority.

revelations.title: A review without remedies is remembrance
revelations.description: A meaningful autumn review must receive evidence and possess defined authority to renew, narrow, replace, compensate, correct, remove, or activate failure succession; discussion alone cannot make temporary power accountable.

clues.title: The Emperor's first prohibition
clues.description: The Emperor refuses to let any Great Clan receive Reedwater whole as a reward for arriving with force. The sentence establishes that service may be honored while governing powers are divided.
clues.discovery: Heard in the opening command; asking whether emergency service creates a claim makes the prohibition explicit.

clues.title: The sword beneath the throne
clues.description: The Emperor says Reedwater needs a sword but that the sword will serve his peace. He leaves open a Great Clan commander serving under an Imperial commission.
clues.discovery: Heard by asking whether the Throne intends to replace every clan soldier with Seppun troops.

clues.title: Seven days and seven proclamations
clues.description: The common holding order expires at the close of the seventh day, and the Emperor requires the Mandate to be carried into Reedwater rather than merely sealed in Otosan Uchi. Each office must have a proclamation and field order naming recipient, route, acknowledgment, and effective hour.
clues.discovery: Heard in the opening command or by asking why the party has seven days rather than a longer court season.

clues.title: Crane relief named before claim
clues.description: The Emperor publicly credits the Crane barges for preventing famine but does not connect that service to ownership. Masuyo therefore has honor she can preserve even if she yields military command.
clues.discovery: Heard in the opening audience; noting the separation between thanks and office is enough.

clues.title: The army held at the ford
clues.description: The Emperor ordered the Lion army to hold rather than withdraw and did not condemn its initial intervention. A bounded commission can therefore be framed as continued service, not forgiveness.
clues.discovery: Heard in the recital of provisional orders or confirmed by a direct procedural question.

clues.title: The flooded shrines named among the losses
clues.description: The Imperial recital lists destroyed shrines and displaced keepers alongside roads and granaries. Sacred restoration is part of the public purpose, not a late Phoenix addition.
clues.discovery: Heard during the opening account; calling attention to the order of losses makes its legal use clear.

clues.title: The Emperor's unanswered question
clues.description: The Emperor asks which clan will yield something it presently holds because Imperial command requires it, not because another clan purchased the concession. The court offers no immediate answer.
clues.discovery: Heard at the end of the opening audience.

clues.title: The Emperor's refusal to count
clues.description: The Emperor states that he can command obedience without a majority and asks instead which proposal can survive the refusal, failure, or misconduct of its strongest supporter.
clues.discovery: Heard if the party frames the opening task as collecting endorsements.

clues.title: The ministry's grain precedent
clues.description: Kazetada produces a precedent in which Crane officials administered harvests under an Imperial title while a different clan held the garrison. The division ended without dishonor after a fixed term.
clues.discovery: Found by asking for a precedent that separates granaries from troops without depicting either party as subordinate.

clues.title: The ministry's two ledgers
clues.description: Otomo practice already separates the ledger of actions from the ledger of review. Kazetada needs a court willing to hear the second ledger without letting it halt every emergency act.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks how Imperial offices are audited without surrendering command.

clues.title: Office without banner
clues.description: Kazetada cites inspectors who served an Imperial ministry while retaining their clan name and no provincial title. Their findings bound the office because dismissal lay elsewhere.
clues.discovery: Found by asking whether the Scorpion can perform the work without visibly receiving Accounts.

clues.title: Four columns beneath each Reed
clues.description: Kazetada’s scribes place title, execution, audit, and succession beneath every office. Any blank column is treated as a political choice rather than an omission.
clues.discovery: Provided when the party accepts ministry drafting assistance.

clues.title: Kazetada's order of presentation
clues.description: Kazetada insists the final presentation begin with the Imperial purpose and acts of obedience, not with a list of supporters. Otherwise the proposal sounds like a coalition imposing terms.
clues.discovery: Given when the party asks how the Emperor will hear the same clauses differently.

clues.title: The three seals never kept together
clues.description: Kazetada shows that stable Imperial provinces keep the powers to feed, coerce, and certify apart even when one governor coordinates them. Their union creates a government able to justify itself.
clues.discovery: Found in the ministry’s comparative office records.

clues.title: The ministry's dead-office precedent
clues.description: Kazetada shows earlier crises in which an office reverted automatically to an Imperial deputy when the holder died or refused an order. The clause prevented a second court crisis.
clues.discovery: Found once the party asks what should have happened after Miya Shigeyuki died.

clues.title: Kazetada's separate obligations
clues.description: Kazetada produces precedents in which one office owes resources to another without surrendering title or execution. A supply obligation can be enforceable without making the beneficiary the owner.
clues.discovery: Found among precedents for Imperial title and clan execution.

clues.title: Kazetada's ungrateful precedent
clues.description: Kazetada separates reimbursement, commendation, and office into three instruments. The Throne may remember and repay service without teaching that service creates jurisdiction.
clues.discovery: Found by asking the Otomo to preserve honor without awarding a Reed.

clues.title: An Otomo precedent for jurisdiction that follows the case
clues.description: Kazetada produces an old commission in which authority passes automatically to a second and third reviewer rather than returning to court for a new appointment.
clues.discovery: Found once the party asks for a conflict rule that cannot be stalled by vacancies.

clues.title: The Otomo note against self-certifying Accounts
clues.description: Kazetada marks any draft in which the office keeping a ledger also controls access, decides discrepancies, and punishes those accused by its own record.
clues.discovery: Seen in the ministry review of the party’s first Accounts clauses.

clues.title: Otomo's rule against invisible double service
clues.description: Kazetada supports one burden register because divided offices become a fiction when all can command the same household without seeing one another’s orders.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking how separation of powers can survive shared provincial resources.

clues.title: Kazetada's prohibition on technical sovereignty
clues.description: Kazetada accepts broad operational discretion but insists that choosing which inhabited district loses Imperial protection is an act of rule and must bear an Imperial author and review.
clues.discovery: Obtained by asking where Otomo division should stop during a flood emergency.

clues.title: Kazetada's recital and operative column
clues.description: Kazetada separates what a ceremony may recite as political consideration from the clause that actually grants or limits power.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking how a public promise should enter the Mandate without becoming an accidental office grant.

clues.title: Kazetada's warning against a seated bloc
clues.description: Kazetada warns that opponents will describe any attractive seating pattern as a permanent faction unless its limited purpose is announced.
clues.discovery: Gained by showing the ministry a proposed moon-viewing arrangement.

clues.title: Kazetada's clause with the courtesy removed
clues.description: Kazetada removes every honorific from a proposed office and finds that no resources, records, or remedy remain beneath the title. He treats the absence as a political allocation, not a scribal gap.
clues.discovery: Received once the party asks the Ministry to simplify an admired clause.

clues.title: Kazetada's coalition with the Emperor removed
clues.description: Kazetada rewrites a proposal as a compact among its supporters. If the clauses still appear to derive authority from their agreement, the architecture has mistaken coalition for Imperial authorship.
clues.discovery: Provided during review of any proposal described primarily by supporting clans.

clues.title: Kazetada's inventory of powers that do not fit in a box
clues.description: Keys and seals occupy one line; current orders, rosters, access rights, debts, protected records, and continuing duties occupy six more. Kazetada treats a surrender without the latter inventory as a change of props.
clues.discovery: Available when a delegation offers a symbol of office as complete submission.

clues.title: The Seppun condition of obedience
clues.description: Tomoe will recommend a Lion commander who lowers the clan standard beneath an Imperial banner, accepts removal, and publishes a withdrawal schedule. She does not demand a powerless command.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking what visible obedience would satisfy the Seppun.

clues.title: The second-breach estimate
clues.description: Seppun reports include Masashige’s estimate that another serious breach may occur within six weeks. The Waters office must be executable before every political dispute is resolved.
clues.discovery: Tomoe shares the estimate when the party asks which threat justifies emergency authority.

clues.title: The empty place before the throne
clues.description: Tomoe reserves a place where clan commanders may lay down checkpoint tokens, standards, or sealed withdrawal schedules before the second audience. The gesture makes obedience visible.
clues.discovery: Shown when the party asks how military submission enters a court proceeding.

clues.title: A commission with an ending
clues.description: Tomoe can describe a limited commission as extraordinary Imperial service completed at review rather than an office taken away after distrust.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party needs a clan to accept time-bounded authority.

clues.title: Command after incapacity
clues.description: Tomoe requires the Sword Reed to name who commands during illness, misconduct inquiry, captured messengers, or conflicting orders. Silence would invite officers to decide legitimacy in the field.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking how a revocable commission functions during the revocation itself.

clues.title: Tomoe's thirty-day variance
clues.description: Tomoe will certify a temporary excess during a named emergency if the amount, expiration, and repayment are entered against the Sword office. The exception answers necessity without transferring Harvest.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking how a fixed quota survives a real military emergency.

clues.title: Tomoe's order of submission
clues.description: Tomoe insists that standards be lowered before the new commission is granted. Obedience must precede office, but the commission may be proclaimed immediately afterward to avoid purposeless humiliation.
clues.discovery: Established by presenting the Lion sequence for Seppun review.

clues.title: Tomoe's removal order with two successors
clues.description: Tomoe refuses to remove a commander into vacancy; her model order invests a temporary successor and names who acts if that successor is conflicted.
clues.discovery: Obtained once the party asks how removal and recusal differ during an emergency.

clues.title: Tomoe's seal for extraordinary force
clues.description: Tomoe will certify force used to evacuate, guard, or open emergency works, but requires the order to name duration, district, and the civil authority choosing any deliberate sacrifice.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking Seppun to support Waters without placing the whole province under a military emergency.

clues.title: Tomoe's refusal of an empty commission
clues.description: Tomoe will publicly refuse a military commission without removal, supply, or replacement rules and immediately state the bounded chain she could accept.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking what kind of public refusal the Seppun would respect.

clues.title: The standard lowered before new orders
clues.description: Tomoe permits a field standard to be lowered only when the recommission, command chain, garrison roster, and first conflicting-order rule are ready to take effect with the gesture.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party prepares military submission for the audience.

clues.title: Tomoe's one messenger, two lawful orders
clues.description: Tomoe presents two valid orders from allied offices and asks which one a field officer obeys. Clan agreement does not resolve command conflict unless the Mandate names precedence or escalation.
clues.discovery: Available once the party claims a cooperative coalition will solve ambiguous authority.

clues.title: The dead governor's divided seals
clues.description: Miya Shun shows that the seven offices once reported through separate seals even though the governor coordinated them. District deputies survived with narrow authority to continue existing duties, but the seal-bearing succession chains died in the compound. Restoring separate lines is administratively possible, not an Otomo invention.
clues.discovery: Found in the preserved dispatch register or offered when the party asks how the offices functioned before the flood.

clues.title: The post roads that survived
clues.description: Miya maps show that Unicorn remount stations kept western messages moving after the Imperial road failed. The network is ready to serve the Mandate immediately.
clues.discovery: Found by comparing dispatch times across the flood line.

clues.title: Four places at the outer screen
clues.description: Miya Shun can admit four provincial witnesses through formal questions and enter their answers in the Imperial record without pretending they hold samurai rank.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks for direct testimony rather than clan summaries.

clues.title: The proclamation test
clues.description: Shun reads each office aloud in the order a herald would proclaim it. Contradictions between public title and daily authority become immediately audible.
clues.discovery: Automatic when a draft is brought from the Chamber to Miya review.

clues.title: The autumn review calendar
clues.description: Shun can schedule reviews after harvest, after the first repaired-dike season, and after the roads reopen, giving each office a performance record rather than an arbitrary expiration.
clues.discovery: Built from the implementation map when the party asks for meaningful review dates.

clues.title: The relief schedule
clues.description: Shun’s schedule shows that ceremonial investiture can wait while grain, medicine, road work, and messenger priority cannot. The Mandate must fund continuity before celebrating it.
clues.discovery: Found by comparing the audience calendar to the delivery calendar.

clues.title: Shun's route-by-route proclamation
clues.description: Shun cannot proclaim a single date of withdrawal across broken roads. He can publish district transfers as each replacement officer arrives, preventing authority from expiring before its successor is present.
clues.discovery: Learned by testing the demobilization calendar against the actual messenger routes.

clues.title: Shun's first proclamation formula
clues.description: Shun drafts separate sentences naming who fed, guarded, rebuilt, and carried the province, followed by the offices each now surrenders or accepts. Exact credit makes equal thanks unnecessary.
clues.discovery: Produced when the party asks for a proclamation that records unequal service without granting ownership.

clues.title: The Miya form with a blank for the keeper
clues.description: Shun refuses to proclaim that consultation occurred unless the implementing notice names the speaker, date, disputed work, decision, and promised remedy.
clues.discovery: Found among the draft village proclamations when the party tests how a Shrines clause travels beyond court.

clues.title: The Miya deadline that needs no second proclamation
clues.description: Shun favors automatic transfer after a stated deadline because villages cannot wait for a second Imperial message whenever a magistrate declines a case.
clues.discovery: Learned by tracing an appeal from a remote district to the capital and back.

clues.title: The Miya proclamation that names the unknown record
clues.description: Shun can proclaim that a sealed report exists, who holds it, what decision it supported, and when it will be reviewed without revealing protected contents.
clues.discovery: Found by asking how secret evidence can remain subject to Imperial memory.

clues.title: Miya form for a taking
clues.description: Shun drafts a proclamation form naming authority, property, condition, value, debtor, repayment date, and petition route. Without those fields the order cannot be repeated consistently district by district.
clues.discovery: Obtained by asking the Miya to turn bounded requisition into language a station keeper can actually use.

clues.title: Shun's correction copy for Reedwater
clues.description: Shun can route authenticated proclamations and corrections to named district witnesses, preventing officeholders from controlling the only text against which their implementation is judged.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking who outside government receives the authoritative version of the Mandate.

clues.title: Shun's sentence before the poem
clues.description: Shun requires every ceremonial meaning to be reducible to one sentence that can later be proclaimed and corrected village by village.
clues.discovery: Discovered while testing a proposed moon-viewing act against the proclamation route.

clues.title: The proclamation that says until
clues.description: Shun insists that gratitude include the event or date until which emergency custody, patrol, transport, or work command was necessary.
clues.discovery: Discovered by testing ceremonial thanks as a village proclamation.

clues.title: Shun's three readings of one order
clues.description: Shun reads a clause as herald, executor, and affected household. Each version requires different knowledge, and only the draft that names authority, burden, record, and petition survives all three.
clues.discovery: Automatic when a draft is prepared for proclamation.

clues.title: The proclamation that opens a petition door
clues.description: Shun writes the first village proclamation to name lawful burdens, the changed commander, the correction route, and the place a petitioner may act before an irreversible loss.
clues.discovery: Available once the party drafts the first public order.

clues.title: Shun's review proclamation with no consequence
clues.description: Shun reads a proclamation announcing that evidence will be heard but cannot say what decision may follow. The province will understand the review as praise, blame, or delay rather than lawful control.
clues.discovery: Found when a review clause names a date but no available disposition.

clues.title: The Reedwater copy that waits for acknowledgment
clues.description: Shun leaves a transfer incomplete until the field copy names what changed hands, which prior orders end, which records accompany it, and who acknowledged receipt. Court delivery starts the chain; field acknowledgment completes it.
clues.discovery: Available in the two-copy transition ledger while planning any transfer.

clues.title: Shun's correction tree for one changed date
clues.description: Moving a transfer date alters courier sequence, holdover authority, replacement orders, supply, proclamation, and petition deadlines. Shun marks every dependent instrument that must be reissued rather than treating the date as local wording.
clues.discovery: Available when a material date, route, recipient, or effective hour changes after drafting.

clues.title: The road days lost to each line of water
clues.description: Shun’s route table prices each dike design in closed bridges, messenger delay, remount changes, isolated districts, and correction time. An engineering line allocates administrative reach as surely as land and flood risk.
clues.discovery: Available when the two designs are read against proclamation and relief routes.

clues.title: Doji Masuyo's careful offer
clues.description: Masuyo will accept Harvest execution without Accounts title and will submit to an outside audit if the Sword cannot rewrite grain orders. Her offer proves a major clan can accept divided powers.
clues.discovery: Gained by separating the Crane demand for recognition from its demand for control.

clues.title: Doji's private line on command
clues.description: Masuyo will concede field command to the Lion if civilian granaries and relief barges remain beyond military reassignment except under a defined emergency.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party treats Harvest and Sword as separate negotiations.

clues.title: The rice that spoiled at a closed ford
clues.description: A Crane barge convoy waited while two emergency authorities disputed a ford toll and escort. The loss demonstrates that access and requisition rules belong in the Roads office.
clues.discovery: Masuyo provides the account when asked where her relief system failed.

clues.title: Doji's borrowed testimony
clues.description: Masuyo intends to present grateful villagers as proof of Crane stewardship. She can be pressed to sponsor their admission while surrendering control over what they say.
clues.discovery: Discovered by asking which witnesses the Crane have already prepared for court.

clues.title: A poem cannot be unsaid
clues.description: Masuyo explains that a poem naming another clan’s burden and one’s own restraint can become the court’s remembered account of a bargain even before a clause exists.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking how the Crane would make a concession visible without signing away leverage.

clues.title: The Crane objection to armed taxation
clues.description: Masuyo argues that the official who commands the soldiers must not be the official who decides how much rice the soldiers cost and seizes it from the granary.
clues.discovery: Heard when the party tests a Lion-centered settlement.

clues.title: The Crane give up the Sword
clues.description: Masuyo can publicly renounce military command if the Lion and Emperor guarantee civilian Harvest. The relinquishment makes the Crane claim narrower and more credible.
clues.discovery: Available once the party offers durable grain protections.

clues.title: The four kinds of rice
clues.description: Masuyo distinguishes household rations, seed rice, the garrison allotment, and emergency reserves. A fixed military quota can protect readiness without letting the commander redefine every storehouse as military supply.
clues.discovery: Learned by attempting to move rice among the seven district basins.

clues.title: Masuyo's price for a shorter term
clues.description: Masuyo will shorten Crane execution of Harvest if the proclamation names the relief, the Accounts office repays documented advances, and Crane wardens may train local successors. Credit can replace duration.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party separates legal tenure from the political record of service.

clues.title: Asahina Chiharu's sealed seed jar
clues.description: Chiharu treats seed rice from a drowned village as an obligation to future households and local shrines. Her testimony gives the Phoenix a concrete sacred boundary within the Harvest settlement.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking why the sealed jar is not included in the district basin.

clues.title: Yorishige's loss account
clues.description: Yorishige names the boats, pilots, temple stores, and private guarantees consumed by relief. Commendation cannot replace a decision about which office repays those losses.
clues.discovery: Produced when the party asks the Crane to forgive its debt for the sake of harmony.

clues.title: The white-cord ledger that audits Crane relief
clues.description: Masuyo accepts outside comparison of Crane-marked grain but insists inspectors cannot reallocate stores merely because they question the account.
clues.discovery: Obtained once the party distinguishes audit of Harvest from execution of Harvest.

clues.title: Yorishige's replacement before credit
clues.description: Yorishige shows that a barge owner can accept delayed repayment while a village that lost its only cart needs replacement before planting. The debt schedule must recognize operational need, not only abstract value.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking which Crane relief creditors can wait and which will cease to exist if they do.

clues.title: The keys given to an office, not a clan
clues.description: Masuyo will present granary keys to a named Harvest titleholder as relinquished custody, but refuses a gesture that gives them back to the Crane as permanent gratitude.
clues.discovery: Gained while designing the public transfer of the southern granaries.

clues.title: Masuyo's credit after the keys leave her hand
clues.description: Masuyo accepts exact public credit most readily when it follows the transfer of granary keys, making honor the consideration for relinquishment rather than proof of continuing title.
clues.discovery: Gained by sequencing Crane honor after civilian custody changes hands.

clues.title: The seed households behind the Harvest gift
clues.description: Chiharu identifies the households and shrine communities whose future depends on seed rice before the court celebrates a new supply or distribution covenant.
clues.discovery: Gained when Harvest generosity could consume the next season.

clues.title: Seed rice reopened by a longer Sword term
clues.description: Extending the garrison commission consumes a later allotment and reopens Crane assent to the supply covenant, the seed reserve, transport priority, and autumn review even though Harvest title is unchanged.
clues.discovery: Established when the party extends Sword without repricing Harvest.

clues.title: The first granary release after the keys change hands
clues.description: Masuyo asks who may open each class of rice the morning after transfer, what ledger proves the release, and where a village petitions an error. The final seal cannot feed anyone until those orders exist.
clues.discovery: Available when the party translates Harvest title and custody into the first distribution cycle.

clues.title: The seed fields on the water design
clues.description: Chiharu overlays both Kaiu designs on seed plots and granary catchments. The cheaper wall protects one season’s stores while salting future fields; the channel saves different villages and moves the planting risk elsewhere.
clues.discovery: Available when the party asks how a Waters design changes Harvest rather than only construction cost.

clues.title: Akodo's acceptable banner
clues.description: Tadanobu will command beneath an Imperial banner if the commission names his authority, duration, and grounds for removal. The Lion objection is to decorative command, not Imperial supremacy.
clues.discovery: Established by offering a concrete commission rather than asking whether the Lion will submit.

clues.title: The Lion's concession on storehouses
clues.description: Tadanobu accepts Crane granary keepers if military supply quotas are fixed in advance and cannot be delayed to influence command. This gives Masuyo a protected civilian role.
clues.discovery: Won by asking the Lion to name the food guarantee it needs rather than demanding control of all granaries.

clues.title: Missing wagons in a complete column
clues.description: Lion supply records show a complete convoy whose grain never reached the listed granary. Tadanobu wants the discrepancy investigated and does not want his own quartermasters to be final judges.
clues.discovery: Disclosed if the party asks what kind of inspection the Lion would accept.

clues.title: Soldiers cannot improvise a dike
clues.description: Tadanobu admits that disciplined labor cannot replace engineering command. He will place soldiers under a Kaiu work schedule if military responsibilities remain explicit.
clues.discovery: Won by asking the Lion to distinguish security competence from engineering competence.

clues.title: The gift returned in full view
clues.description: Tadanobu notes that accepting or returning a military gift before the court can acknowledge command, limit it, or reject the relationship entirely.
clues.discovery: Discovered while planning what symbol the Lion could accept beneath an Imperial commission.

clues.title: A general's own warning
clues.description: Tadanobu admits that an army controlling its own food assessment and accounts can describe every expansion as necessity. He prefers guaranteed supply to fiscal possession.
clues.discovery: Won by asking which power a disciplined commander should not want.

clues.title: The Lion give up the Harvest
clues.description: Tadanobu can renounce control of civilian granaries in exchange for fixed supply and a real Sword commission. His surrender answers the fear of armed taxation.
clues.discovery: Available once supply cannot be manipulated by the granary holder.

clues.title: Tadanobu's declining roster
clues.description: Tadanobu offers a supply schedule that falls automatically as companies depart. He wants a right to the stated allotment, not authority to assess the granaries that provide it.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks how military supply changes during demobilization.

clues.title: The six stages of departure
clues.description: Tadanobu can lower standards, surrender granary keys, release roads, recommission a core force, replace the rest district by district, and submit to autumn review. Each stage resolves a different danger.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking the Lion to draft withdrawal as an operation rather than an ultimatum.

clues.title: Kiyoka's eleven villages
clues.description: Matsu Kiyoka has eleven written requests for continued protection. Named replacements let her obey without arguing that the court has ordered the Lion to abandon those who relied upon it.
clues.discovery: Disclosed when the party asks which duties, rather than territories, keep Lion troops in place.

clues.title: Noritada's history of obedience
clues.description: Ikoma Noritada can describe the Lion deployment as order restored and strength placed beneath Imperial command. That account lets the army leave positions it no longer legally owns.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking what exact sentence would make demobilization honorable.

clues.title: The commander who refuses the granary
clues.description: Tadanobu expressly rejects Harvest and Accounts while demanding enforceable supply. His position demonstrates that strong execution can coexist with deliberately divided reinforcing powers.
clues.discovery: Won by asking which authority a disciplined general should decline.

clues.title: Noritada's autumn ending
clues.description: Noritada can present the autumn review as the appointed completion of an Imperial campaign rather than a later judgment that the Lion should never have served.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking how the Lion would narrate a reduced force after the harvest.

clues.title: Kiyoka's soldiers in the mud
clues.description: Kiyoka offers soldiers for dangerous heavy work if their contribution reduces civilian calls and enters the same ledger rather than becoming an argument for more Lion authority.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks whether the garrison can discharge burdens as well as impose them.

clues.title: The standard fitting that does not command
clues.description: Noritada proposes an honor made from a retired standard fitting, preserving the history of Lion service without presenting a command emblem to the future Sword holder.
clues.discovery: Available if the party seeks to honor the Lion without confusing memory and commission.

clues.title: Noritada's history ending at recommission
clues.description: Noritada can narrate Lion emergency service as complete when the standards lower and a smaller force receives an Imperial commission, preserving continuity without permanent mobilized authority.
clues.discovery: Available while preparing the public history of demobilization.

clues.title: Tadanobu's roster behind the red cloth
clues.description: Tadanobu provides the officers, patrols, stores, messengers, and pending commands that must transfer with any lowered standard. Without the roster, the symbol leaves the field army unchanged.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking what practical command the Lion will surrender or accept under commission.

clues.title: The first patrol order after the standard lowers
clues.description: Tadanobu asks who issues the next dawn patrol, from which roster, under what supply, and with what rule for a conflicting old command. A Mandate that answers only who holds the Sword on paper has not begun government.
clues.discovery: Available when visible submission is converted into the first day of recommissioned command.

clues.title: The garrison term that reopens rice and relief
clues.description: Extending one company’s term changes the declining allotment, replacement roster, village release, public thanks, and autumn review. Tadanobu accepts the change only after every dependent promise is called back to the table.
clues.discovery: Available if the party lengthens or shortens the Sword settlement after dependent concessions.

clues.title: The villages beneath the declining roster
clues.description: Each company kept for another month needs rice, quarters, patrol roads, replacement labor, and households subject to its orders. Kiyoka makes the party enter those payers before calling an extended deployment a narrow concession.
clues.discovery: Available when the party adjusts garrison duration or replacement without reopening the burden ledger.

clues.title: Isawa's demand for a neutral appeal
clues.description: Etsuko will accept engineering decisions over ritual objections if the office making the decision cannot also be the final judge of whether consultation was adequate.
clues.discovery: Gained by presenting a real conflict between a dike line and a shrine boundary.

clues.title: The river kami and the new channel
clues.description: Etsuko confirms that ritual alone will not return the river to its old course. Material reconstruction is spiritually necessary, though its route still carries obligations.
clues.discovery: Established through consultation with the local-water records and the recovered bells.

clues.title: The ritual order of cups
clues.description: Etsuko can arrange the serving order so public thanks follow the actual sequence of burdens rather than clan rank alone. The sequence creates witnesses without making law.
clues.discovery: Offered if the party asks the Phoenix to shape the evening rather than merely bless it.

clues.title: The three bells that name three claimants
clues.description: Etsuko shows that identifying a sacred site does not identify who may bind it: a surviving keeper, a displaced community, and a specialist can each speak to different parts of the obligation.
clues.discovery: Learned once the party answers which recovered bell should be rung first and why.

clues.title: Etsuko's sealed name and public duty
clues.description: Etsuko will conceal the identity of a vulnerable keeper while still stating the site, duty, decision, remedy, and reviewer in the public Shrines record.
clues.discovery: Offered when a displaced keeper fears retaliation from the office seeking the land.

clues.title: Etsuko's protected route for a frightened keeper
clues.description: Etsuko will use a protected Scorpion reporting channel for a keeper who fears the office seeking shrine land, provided an outside reviewer can test the report without exposing the source automatically.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks how sacred consultation can survive intimidation.

clues.title: The Phoenix commission that ends when two keepers are ready
clues.description: Chise proposes that imported Phoenix execution expire when two local successors per district are trained and the autumn panel confirms which duties remain unfinished.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking what success, rather than a calendar alone, would end Phoenix authority.

clues.title: Chise's list of people who kept the shrines before court arrived
clues.description: Chise demonstrates that Reedwater households held continuing ritual duties before any Great Clan commission and therefore deserve standing beyond ceremonial testimony.
clues.discovery: Found in the copied village registers and keeper lists.

clues.title: The blessing that waits for the relocation ledger
clues.description: Etsuko will not bless a reconstruction compact until it assigns the labor, compensation, replacement sites, and dates created by its sacred concessions.
clues.discovery: Learned once the party asks for Phoenix approval before settling who bears the cost.

clues.title: The shrine calendar inside the labor calendar
clues.description: Koremori shows that ritual and funerary service removes named people on fixed days; treating that duty as leisure leaves both shrines and work camps without the people expected to serve them.
clues.discovery: Obtained by asking whether sacred obligations can be entered as actual scheduling constraints.

clues.title: Etsuko's question of which obligation moves
clues.description: Etsuko accepts that sacred sites may yield, then asks which households, graves, rites, stipends, and restoration duties move with them. The engineering line distributes spiritual and social costs.
clues.discovery: Obtained by presenting either major dike design for sacred consultation.

clues.title: The restoration debt after bypass
clues.description: Koremori accepts immediate action when delay threatens lives if the bypass automatically records restoration, reconsultation, and review rather than allowing emergency necessity to erase the affected obligation.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party tests sacred consultation against a rapidly failing dike.

clues.title: The cups served by burden, not alliance
clues.description: Etsuko can order cups by the sequence of obligations borne, allowing cooperation to be visible without claiming spiritual or political unity among the guests.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks the Phoenix to distinguish ritual sequence from endorsement.

clues.title: Etsuko's northern channel instead
clues.description: Etsuko refuses to bless a route through an unexamined sacred community but offers a dawn consultation on the northern channel rather than treating all construction as forbidden.
clues.discovery: Discovered when a proposed public blessing outruns the consultation already completed.

clues.title: The Phoenix commission reviewed by capacity
clues.description: Chise proposes that review determine whether local keepers are trained, which duties remain unfinished, and whether the outside commission ends, narrows, or continues with a specific remedy for withheld transfer.
clues.discovery: Available once the party turns sacred succession into a review standard.

clues.title: The shrine clause with four visible debts
clues.description: Etsuko rejects a clause that merely orders consultation. She requires a named decision-maker, the households and labor carrying the delay, a remedy after emergency bypass, and a record that follows the site into review.
clues.discovery: Available when the party reduces the Phoenix charter to an operative Shrines clause.

clues.title: The village that performs the court's sacred compromise
clues.description: A compromise between Phoenix and Crab may still require displaced keepers to travel, rebuild, maintain rites, and absorb delay. Chise names the households before the court congratulates the offices that negotiated over them.
clues.discovery: Available when a sacred accommodation assigns labor or relocation to people absent from the bargain.

clues.title: Kitsuki's distinction between command and possession
clues.description: Harunori distinguishes operational command from ownership of the office and from the right to appoint a successor. A clan can wield the Sword without possessing it permanently.
clues.discovery: Obtained once the party asks which parts of military authority must remain joined.

clues.title: A Kitsuki record of sacred boundaries
clues.description: Harunori preserved maps showing that several proposed dike lines cross lands held in trust for shrines. The boundaries can be altered, but not treated as ownerless mud.
clues.discovery: Found in the Reedwater claim record when the party asks which reconstruction choices create legal disputes.

clues.title: The appeal path in red ink
clues.description: Harunori marks every place where an executor, auditor, and judge belong to the same interest. His red path shows where recusal or Imperial appeal must enter.
clues.discovery: Received once the party requests a structural review rather than endorsement.

clues.title: The successor clause
clues.description: Harunori distinguishes ordinary succession from failure succession: the person who inherits a title need not be the person who acts when the titleholder is accused or absent.
clues.discovery: Offered during review of any draft that names only one successor.

clues.title: Two drafts, one duty
clues.description: Harunori says two complete proposals can serve one Imperial command if both answer the same stated purpose and their differences are disclosed rather than hidden as rival loyalties.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party worries that maintaining a fallback appears duplicitous.

clues.title: Harunori's boundary between theology and procedure
clues.description: Harunori will review notice, standing, reasons, recusal, and remedy without claiming that a magistrate can decide whether the kami truly spoke.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks how Judgment can review Shrines without subordinating religion to law.

clues.title: The central stone crowded with recused judges
clues.description: Harunori demonstrates that every office can disable Judgment if conflicts merely remove magistrates without transferring authority to named substitutes.
clues.discovery: Revealed through the seven-tablet exercise at the opening of the audience.

clues.title: Harunori's chain of custody before judgment
clues.description: Harunori will act on an inspector’s report only if the record shows what was accessed, copied, sealed, altered, and transferred before it reached Judgment.
clues.discovery: Gained by presenting a discrepancy whose original ledger remains with the accused office.

clues.title: Harunori's expiration date on a sealed record
clues.description: Harunori accepts sealed identities and military details only when the record names who may review them and when continued secrecy must be justified again.
clues.discovery: Received during review of any clause that says merely “confidential.”

clues.title: Harunori's record of the chosen risk
clues.description: Harunori proposes that the deciding authority record rejected alternatives and affected claimants so a later failure cannot be described as an engineer’s unexplained error.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks how Judgment can review a technical choice without pretending to engineer.

clues.title: Sorin's petition the sponsor cannot withdraw
clues.description: Sorin proposes that sponsorship provide access and protection while the petition remains the claimant’s, so a patron cannot silence testimony once it ceases to flatter the patron.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks how low-status claimants can appear without becoming political property.

clues.title: Harunori's two moonlit records
clues.description: Harunori proposes recording both the exact public words and the meaning the parties stated before speaking, preserving evidence of later expansion or denial.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks how Judgment could decide what the court actually witnessed.

clues.title: The empty place for the substitute judge
clues.description: Harunori suggests an empty cushion before Judgment to make substitute jurisdiction visible without pretending a particular candidate has already been accepted.
clues.discovery: Discovered while translating recusal into a public image.

clues.title: Harunori's amendment chain
clues.description: Changing who certifies the end of a commission also changes recusal, appeal, interim authority, and the evidence required at review. Harunori refuses to call the amendment local.
clues.discovery: Received once the party alters a term or certifier during legal review.

clues.title: Harunori's failed-supporter test
clues.description: Harunori removes the most cooperative titleholder from the draft and traces whether audit, appeal, resources, and failure succession still function. Approval is useful evidence, not structural resilience.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking how the Emperor will test a popular proposal.

clues.title: Harunori's review that can change the order
clues.description: Harunori distinguishes a commemorative hearing from review by asking who may stay, narrow, replace, compensate, reopen, or terminate the challenged power. A forum unable to alter consequence can only write history.
clues.discovery: Available when the party tests an autumn review or appeal clause against an actual failed office.

clues.title: A Bayushi compliment on weakness
clues.description: Namika praises a mandate no clan can generously carry alone. Beneath the compliment is an endorsement of Otomo-style division as protection against self-certifying power.
clues.discovery: Heard in private after the party asks which settlement the Scorpion would be least able to exploit.

clues.title: Bayushi's objection to self-inspection
clues.description: Namika says an inspector appointed, paid, and dismissible by the inspected office is a courtier carrying a decorative ledger. She supports external review even when the Scorpion hold execution.
clues.discovery: Heard when the party offers the Scorpion an office that audits itself.

clues.title: A customs promise with teeth
clues.description: Namika will accept a toll ceiling and open roads if inspectors can compare manifests at every crossing. The Scorpion condition makes Unicorn stewardship auditable rather than private.
clues.discovery: Offered in response to a concrete Unicorn Roads proposal.

clues.title: The role written for a rival
clues.description: Namika can write a performance in which a rival speaks the exact limitation it privately accepts while appearing generous rather than cornered.
clues.discovery: Available if the party shares the real concession and the face the rival must preserve.

clues.title: The Scorpion give up the title
clues.description: Namika can publicly relinquish Accounts title while retaining narrow inspection. The concession helps other clans accept Scorpion involvement without pretending the work is unnecessary.
clues.discovery: Available if protected reporting and manifest access are secured.

clues.title: A proposal kept folded
clues.description: Namika advises the party to let opponents know a fallback exists without revealing every clause. The threat must be credible enough to change bargaining and lawful enough to survive exposure.
clues.discovery: Gained in private after the party has at least one complete alternative.

clues.title: Namika's question about the accused inspector
clues.description: Namika asks who receives a complaint against an inspector when the ordinary reviewer appointed that inspector and may dismiss her, forcing the Mandate to name a substitute forum.
clues.discovery: Raised after the party gives Accounts protected independence.

clues.title: Namika's six verbs for inspection
clues.description: Namika separates access, comparison, preservation, reporting, restraint, and sanction, then asks the party to assign each power rather than grant a single undefined right to inspect.
clues.discovery: Presented when the party drafts the Accounts office in concrete verbs.

clues.title: Mirei's five rungs of secrecy
clues.description: Mirei distinguishes public rules, confidential sources, sealed interim findings, reviewable findings, and public dispositions, each with a custodian and deadline.
clues.discovery: Learned once the party asks whether the Scorpion demand that all inspection remain secret.

clues.title: The inspector's unpaid receipt index
clues.description: Kureha can compare numbered receipts across offices and identify repeated taking, altered valuation, and debts shifted to defunct commands, provided inspectors preserve the record without setting compensation themselves.
clues.discovery: Offered when Accounts inspection is paired with a public requisition schedule.

clues.title: Mirei's protected return witness
clues.description: Mirei can protect identities or travel during implementation while preserving testable substance for the autumn review, provided secrecy does not let inspectors substitute themselves for the witness.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking how Reedwater testimony survives retaliation after the court disperses.

clues.title: The mask accepted for inspection alone
clues.description: Namika can accept a mask of vigilance as a bounded inspection duty while publicly declining title, execution, custody, and sanction in Accounts.
clues.discovery: Offered if the party separates the Scorpion role before the public exchange.

clues.title: Namika's title declined, duty accepted
clues.description: Namika can refuse the visible title of Accounts while accepting comparison, preservation, and protected reporting under outside custody and review.
clues.discovery: Offered if the party gives the Scorpion a narrower lawful path than officeholding.

clues.title: The relief debt closed without an office
clues.description: Scorpion comparison can certify a relief debt for payment and public acknowledgment while marking that the settlement conveys no jurisdiction over the office involved.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking Accounts inspection to distinguish compensation from future authority.

clues.title: Custody that cannot correct the public record
clues.description: Mirei shows how an inspector may possess accurate records while a false tax order remains public. Without a correction route and final authority, record access is knowledge without government.
clues.discovery: Available once the party assigns inspection but omits public correction.

clues.title: The ledger delivered with divided access
clues.description: Namika offers record custody, protected-source access, final reporting, and sanction as separate transfers. Delivering the box without the access rules would merely move hidden authority to another room.
clues.discovery: Established when the party prepares the open-ledger submission.

clues.title: The road master's schedule
clues.description: Sachiko has a district-by-district route showing which orders can travel by remount, barge, temple messenger, or caravan. Miya implementation can be built on this network.
clues.discovery: Shared in exchange for including road access and messenger priority in the draft.

clues.title: Three customs books
clues.description: Unicorn, Crane, and emergency customs ledgers record different quantities for the same caravans. The disagreement is public and ordinary enough to require standing inspection rather than a dramatic accusation.
clues.discovery: Sachiko lays out the books when asked why roads and Accounts cannot be negotiated separately.

clues.title: The caravan master's invitation
clues.description: Sachiko offers Saburo a place under Unicorn hospitality, giving him protection from dismissal as a mere merchant while leaving his testimony his own.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking the Unicorn to sponsor access rather than dictate content.

clues.title: Road stewardship by season
clues.description: Sachiko will accept temporary execution of Roads if renewal depends on public measures of travel time, tolls, and compensated requisitions.
clues.discovery: Offered in response to a proposal that avoids permanent Unicorn title.

clues.title: The Unicorn duplicate manifest at every crossing
clues.description: Sachiko will accept common manifests and outside comparison if inspectors cannot seize routine cargo or set toll policy by opening an inquiry.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party pairs Scorpion access with Unicorn Roads execution.

clues.title: The horse requisitioned three times
clues.description: Sachiko produces three lawful receipts for successive claims on the same household mare. None records the earlier service, the animal’s condition, or the office that owes replacement.
clues.discovery: Entered automatically when the party asks why a general promise of later compensation will not keep the western road functioning.

clues.title: The road cut by mercy
clues.description: Nergui shows that the northern channel preserves villages while cutting the west road and requiring new stations, horses, and a ford. A humane water choice transfers burden into movement.
clues.discovery: Gained by placing the Waters drawings over the Unicorn route board.

clues.title: Remount bells and the drivers behind them
clues.description: Sachiko notes that giving horses or remount bells as an undertaking also assigns handlers, fodder, return dates, and replacement debt unless the gift is carefully bounded.
clues.discovery: Discovered when ceremonial generosity includes transport resources.

clues.title: The carts inside the generous route
clues.description: Sachiko identifies the drivers, animals, station keepers, fodder, delays, and replacement debt hidden inside a promise to provide transport.
clues.discovery: Discovered when a Roads concession is described only as clan generosity.

clues.title: Checkpoint tokens returned with the requisition books
clues.description: Sachiko will return road tokens only with the requisition books, current debts, route orders, and messenger roster. Transferring the token alone would preserve every practical dependency in Unicorn hands.
clues.discovery: Available when Roads submission is reduced to a ceremonial object.

clues.title: The horses assigned to the first orders
clues.description: Boroldai asks which remounts, couriers, closures, and priority categories carry the new Mandate before the next rain. An order without movement resources reaches only the capital.
clues.discovery: Established when the party asks whether implementation can begin immediately.

clues.title: The road clearance that proves a garrison has left
clues.description: Boroldai counts released checkpoints, returned carts, reopened crossings, canceled requisitions, and messengers carrying the new command. Troops may march away while occupation survives in road control and unpaid taking.
clues.discovery: Available when Roads verifies a stage of military withdrawal.

clues.title: Kaiu's emergency chain
clues.description: Masashige proposes work-site guards under a clan officer who reports through the Waters commission to Seppun emergency authority. The arrangement supplies force without granting a private garrison.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party asks who protects labor camps during reconstruction.

clues.title: The Kaiu chain of work camps
clues.description: Masashige needs one military chain to secure quarries and camps. He prefers a competent Lion commission to several ceremonial commanders issuing conflicting orders.
clues.discovery: Obtained by asking which military arrangement lets work begin immediately.

clues.title: Kaiu's refusal to build through a shrine
clues.description: Masashige has an alternate dike line that preserves the largest shrine boundary at higher cost. He needs a political decision about money and land, not permission to ignore the shrine.
clues.discovery: Revealed when the party requests more than one engineering plan.

clues.title: Kaiu's demand to hear the laborers
clues.description: Masashige refuses to finalize a work levy without hearing who has already been conscripted elsewhere. His technical need creates a respectable route for village testimony.
clues.discovery: Offered once the party requests a defensible labor schedule.

clues.title: Kaiu's list before banners
clues.description: Masashige demands quarries, timber, food, guards, labor, and authority be named before the court debates whose mon appears on the completed dike.
clues.discovery: Entered automatically when the party asks him to endorse a ceremonial allocation.

clues.title: Kaiu stakes around an unmarked shrine
clues.description: Masashige can route works around a protected site only if someone marks the boundary before labor begins and accepts responsibility for delay, relocation, or override.
clues.discovery: Obtained by asking which spiritual promises an engineer can actually build around.

clues.title: Chihaya's names, not bodies
clues.description: Chihaya refuses a quota stated only as three hundred laborers and asks which households already supply soldiers, carts, shrine service, or granary work and who will plant while they are absent.
clues.discovery: Entered automatically when the party asks the Crab to reduce a technical schedule to a provincial quota.

clues.title: Masashige's two honest maps
clues.description: The eastern-wall and northern-channel maps each mark protected districts, delayed districts, displaced communities, road loss, labor, and materials rather than displaying only structural measurements.
clues.discovery: Entered automatically when the party asks which design is technically best and Masashige refuses the premise.

clues.title: The three levels of emergency work
clues.description: Masashige separates site safety, plan-preserving emergency action, and political sacrifice, granting the executor speed without letting flood, shrine, seed, or route choices disappear into engineering discretion.
clues.discovery: Entered automatically when the party asks for a bounded emergency clause.

clues.title: Masashige's refusal to inherit another's shortage
clues.description: Masashige refuses responsibility for a design whose labor and materials another office can withhold, then accepts execution if the shared burden ledger and protected stockpile are named.
clues.discovery: Available once the party asks him to accept Waters under incomplete resource clauses.

clues.title: The district sacrificed by the beautiful dike
clues.description: Masashige names the district, road, graves, and planting time transferred by each engineering plan before accepting ceremonial praise for reconstruction.
clues.discovery: Available when the court treats technical agreement as burden-free.

clues.title: Kameyo's price for a merciful amendment
clues.description: A change that preserves one village requires another bridge, more timber, longer road closure, and additional labor. Kameyo records the linked promises that must be reopened before mercy is purchased with absent resources.
clues.discovery: Automatic when an engineering amendment changes land, route, or schedule.

clues.title: Masashige's clause read against the work yard
clues.description: Masashige traces a proposed Waters clause against crews, stores, displaced households, emergency choices, repair duties, and inspection books. Any power not paired with its burden, remedy, and record fails before the first timber moves.
clues.discovery: Available when the party asks whether a Waters clause can actually be executed.

clues.title: Rei's test of a law
clues.description: Rei says a quota without a named collector, date, and appeal becomes whatever the arriving official claims. Her test converts courtly ambiguity into an implementation failure.
clues.discovery: Gained by reading a proposed clause aloud and allowing her to ask who will appear at the village gate.

clues.title: The granary keys
clues.description: Reed Bank trusted the Crane relief clerks because distributions were recorded at the door. The villagers fear soldiers changing the entries after the grain has left.
clues.discovery: Rei shows the copied distribution sticks when asked which emergency system actually worked.

clues.title: Brother Hojun's drowned bells
clues.description: Hojun explains that moving a bell is easy; moving the households whose calendar, burials, and water rites gather around it is not. Compensation alone does not restore the obligation.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking what would be lost if the shrine were rebuilt on convenient higher ground.

clues.title: The horses that did not return
clues.description: Saburo lists animals requisitioned by three different authorities, none of which accepts the debt. A compensation schedule is necessary if local transport is to survive Imperial service.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking what the emergency roads consumed rather than only what they delivered.

clues.title: The names on the work levy
clues.description: Rei shows that current labor demands call the same households to Crane unloading, Lion patrol support, and Crab work camps. One Waters authority must coordinate or cancel overlapping levies.
clues.discovery: Found by comparing village duty sticks rather than accepting each office’s total separately.

clues.title: Rei's arithmetic
clues.description: Rei totals labor days, seed rice, cart animals, and displaced households before asking which clan receives thanks. The numbers expose honors financed by unassigned provincial burdens.
clues.discovery: Gained by allowing her to compare all current emergency demands on one village.

clues.title: Rei counts next year's hunger
clues.description: Rei explains that soldiers and villagers can both survive this month by consuming seed rice, leaving both to starve after planting. A valid covenant must state which store the military quota may reach.
clues.discovery: Established by asking the headwoman which shortages a courtly total conceals.

clues.title: Kenta's empty patrol roster
clues.description: Kenta can name the dead and missing provincial officers whose duties the Lion assumed. Withdrawal without a replacement roster restores offices on paper while leaving their roads unguarded.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking what local authority actually remains beneath the clan deployments.

clues.title: Hojun's register of the displaced keepers
clues.description: Hojun has the names of families who maintained local sites and the camps where they now live, proving that consultation can reach them if the court chooses to pay the cost.
clues.discovery: Shared when the party asks whether Reedwater has any surviving authority below the Great Clans.

clues.title: Saburo's four kinds of repayment
clues.description: Saburo distinguishes coin, tax credit, replacement in kind, and future trade priority, showing that a remedy useful to a caravan association may be worthless to a one-horse farming household.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking whether acknowledging the debt is enough without specifying its form and date.

clues.title: Rei's one ledger for seven Reeds
clues.description: Rei enters every service demand against the same households and reveals that each office’s individually plausible levy depends on labor already promised elsewhere.
clues.discovery: Established by holding the burden hearing and refusing to total each Reed separately.

clues.title: The village that is safer and poorer
clues.description: Rei calculates that higher relocation ground reduces flood risk but yields less rice and worse road access. Safety cannot be counted without livelihood and time.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking whether relocation to higher ground fully compensates Reed Bank.

clues.title: Rei's demand for the name on the breach
clues.description: Rei will accept that one district may be flooded to save several, but asks which official chooses, what evidence existed, who warns the district, and what debt follows the water.
clues.discovery: Gained by asking the witnesses to endorse broad emergency authority in the abstract.

clues.title: The five rights after the hearing
clues.description: The witnesses ask for receipt of proclamations, access to burden entries, petitions not owned by sponsors, objective review triggers, and required return testimony before commissions renew.
clues.discovery: Automatic if the party asks what the witnesses need after leaving the capital.

clues.title: The witness facing the burden, not the patron
clues.description: Rei insists that Reedwater witnesses be placed opposite the offices changing their lives rather than beside the courtiers who sponsored their admission.
clues.discovery: Gained by inviting the witnesses to review the seating plan.

clues.title: Rei's question about tomorrow's labor
clues.description: Rei asks which households work tomorrow under a celebrated engineering or transport agreement, forcing the ceremonial duty into the common burden ledger.
clues.discovery: Gained by bringing a proposed public bargain to the provincial witnesses.

clues.title: The household named after the order
clues.description: Rei demonstrates that a lawful labor call can still be incomplete when the burden ledger, exemption route, and appeal forum are absent. Naming the household makes the missing institutions visible.
clues.discovery: Established when the party tests a clause against one actual Reedwater household.

clues.title: Rei's first week of petitions
clues.description: Rei lists the labor calls, displacement claims, seed disputes, and missing compensation that will arrive in the first week. A review scheduled for autumn cannot substitute for an immediate forum.
clues.discovery: Received once the party tests its implementation calendar against current provincial harms.

clues.title: The provincial chair that can trigger replacement
clues.description: Rei accepts advisory standing only when documented burden or failed transfer can trigger correction, compensation, narrowed authority, or failure succession rather than another respectful hearing.
clues.discovery: Established when the party asks what provincial standing accomplishes at review.

clues.title: Kenta's two names beneath each Reed
clues.description: Kenta writes a competent provincial successor and a separate officer empowered to act if that successor is absent, accused, or incapacitated. Blank second lines expose offices whose succession merely recreates paralysis.
clues.discovery: Available when Kenta tests whether a provincial succession compact still functions after recusal, failed receipt, or incapacity.

clues.title: The mask offered without a seat
clues.description: Namika publicly offers the Scorpion mask of vigilance while praising another clan as the face of Accounts. The performance lets her claim inspection without demanding the visible office.
clues.discovery: Created if the party gives Namika a role in the evening that honors service while assigning title elsewhere.

clues.title: The Emperor's cup left empty
clues.description: The ceremonial sequence reserves the first cup for the Emperor and leaves it unfilled until the clans name what they will surrender to his peace. The omission makes Imperial authorship visible without requiring the Emperor to bargain in public.
clues.discovery: Created if the party and the ritual officers arrange the evening around obedience before reward.

clues.title: Promises brought in from moonlight
clues.description: Public concessions made during the moon-viewing can be indexed as side covenants or recitals, preserving face without confusing ceremonial words with operative clauses.
clues.discovery: Available after a witnessed bargain if the party records exactly what was and was not promised.

clues.title: The keys beneath white and red
clues.description: The Crane can present granary keys beneath white silk while the Lion lowers red standards beneath an Imperial banner. The paired acts give both clans visible honor precisely through the powers they relinquish.
clues.discovery: Available if the party stages both concessions as one witnessed exchange.

clues.title: The masked recitation of each emergency exemption
clues.description: Mirei can make the categories of exemption public through masked roles while keeping individual sources and unresolved accusations out of the performance.
clues.discovery: Available if the party uses the evening to secure consent for common records rather than expose culprits.

clues.title: The nine lines of the ceremonial docket
clues.description: Shun refuses to stage an obligation until its act, authority, scope, term, third parties, witnesses, refusal path, and operative follow-up are written in plain language.
clues.discovery: Available while preparing any public act for the evening.

clues.title: Four meanings for one offered object
clues.description: Sachiko distinguishes gifts of repayment, honor, custody, and undertaking before any object enters the garden.
clues.discovery: Available while selecting or receiving a ceremonial gift.

clues.title: The pools faced together for one bargain
clues.description: The party can place delegates beside or opposite the Reeds they must settle together while Harunori records that the arrangement concerns one bargain rather than every office.
clues.discovery: Available while arranging the garden.

clues.title: Five forms of no beneath the moon
clues.description: The evening recognizes correction, narrow acceptance, substitution, witnessed refusal, and withdrawal, each preserving a path back to lawful drafting.
clues.discovery: Available whenever a participant cannot accept the staged meaning.

clues.title: Thanks with a date and a release
clues.description: Shun will announce service, compensation, transfer, and the date on which the emergency claim becomes ordinary commissioned duty or ends.
clues.discovery: Available while drafting any public thanks.

clues.title: The third party named before applause
clues.description: Reedwater witnesses may interrupt an exchange before applause to name the households, routes, shrines, records, or successors whose burden the court has omitted.
clues.discovery: Available whenever a public bargain assigns resources or risk beyond the speakers.

clues.title: The moonlit concession with a missing condition
clues.description: A public promise survives as memory after its intended clause changes, but its operative force does not. The speakers must reaffirm, narrow, replace, or release the promise before applause becomes law.
clues.discovery: Found when a public obligation is imported into a materially different draft.

clues.title: The two surrenders announced as one peace
clues.description: Shun will pair concessions only when each party gives up a power it presently holds and neither act is described as payment for the other party’s obedience. The court can honor both without declaring either victor.
clues.discovery: Available while staging a reciprocal public bargain or correcting one framed as a purchase.

clues.title: The blank proclamation columns
clues.description: Miya scribes leave date, route, recipient, and correction columns blank beside every elegant clause that cannot yet be proclaimed. The blanks reveal whether the Mandate is executable.
clues.discovery: Entered automatically when the party submits a draft to the Chamber.

clues.title: The empty appeal clause
clues.description: Every draft initially names duties and penalties more readily than a forum for appeal. Harunori offers a circuit with recusals and a direct Imperial review for conflicts among Reeds.
clues.discovery: Automatic when a draft assigns enforcement without an appeal path.

clues.title: The first line of the Mandate
clues.description: The scribes propose beginning, “By Our concern for Reedwater and Our peace among the Clans,” rather than naming the parties who negotiated the settlement. The line preserves Imperial authorship without erasing their service.
clues.discovery: Automatic during final drafting unless the party chooses a rival framing.

clues.title: The fallback seal-string
clues.description: The Chamber keeps a different cord and seal order for the second draft, forcing the party to identify which supporters and relinquishments truly belong to it.
clues.discovery: Entered automatically when the party attempts to maintain two proposals.

clues.title: The autumn chair reserved for consequence
clues.description: A draft clause reserves testimony from district witnesses before any commission is renewed, ensuring that successful court access becomes an implementation check rather than a ceremonial exception.
clues.discovery: Found once the party writes the autumn review participants before deciding which offices will be renewed.

clues.title: The Chamber's margin for public words
clues.description: The drafting forms preserve public recitals in a margin beside operative clauses so a concession can retain political force without silently enlarging legal authority.
clues.discovery: Available when importing a witnessed obligation into a draft.

clues.title: The tenth strip beneath the nine boxes
clues.description: The Chamber places title, execution, audit, resources, emergency power, succession, term, and review in separate boxes, then lays one crosswise strip for remedy. Any office lacking the strip is marked as capable of commanding but not of answering.
clues.discovery: Entered automatically when the party completes its first Reed matrix.

clues.title: The red cords that move with the clause
clues.description: Harunori ties supply, roads, sacred procedure, burdens, records, and succession to the clauses they depend on. Moving one material term physically drags a web of obligations across the table.
clues.discovery: Automatic during the dependency pass in the Chamber.

clues.title: The first-forty-days bundle
clues.description: The Chamber refuses certification until the draft includes changed field orders, transfer dates, provisional pay and stores, public notices, petition routes, and initial compliance checks.
clues.discovery: Automatic after the seven office matrices are complete.

clues.title: The review box that must contain a disposition
clues.description: The Chamber will not accept a review field containing only participants and a date. The box must name evidence, standards, interim protection, and at least one power capable of changing the office.
clues.discovery: Automatic when a Reed matrix reaches its review field.

clues.title: The effective hour in the submission register
clues.description: Tomoe records the exact hour at which each key, standard, token, ledger, or seal changes legal status, together with the receiving field officer, courier and acknowledgment route, inventory, continuing duty, and remedy for incomplete transfer.
clues.discovery: Automatic when the first act of submission is presented.

clues.title: The messenger who leaves before the court
clues.description: The Emperor asks which new order reaches Reedwater tomorrow and dispatches an authenticated copy to its named receiving officer before the audience disperses. A proposal unable to answer remains a judgment about autumn rather than a present government.
clues.discovery: Automatic during the transition movement of the final audience.

clues.title: The question after the last seal
clues.description: After every delegation has been named, the Emperor asks who feeds the soldiers, audits the collector, halts the engineer, and acts after recusal. The seals do not answer any of these questions.
clues.discovery: Entered automatically when the party finishes presenting the Seven Reeds.

clues.title: The autumn review with seven possible verbs
clues.description: The Emperor asks whether the autumn panel may renew, narrow, replace, compensate, correct, remove, or activate failure succession. If it may only hear reports, the term is politically permanent until another crisis.
clues.discovery: Entered automatically when the party presents its review clauses.

clues.title: The Emperor's question in the bare margin
clues.description: For any clause the party praises, the Emperor asks who pays, who repairs harm, who keeps the record, and who can compel an answer. A clause missing one returns to the broad sheet, however many delegations sealed it.
clues.discovery: Available during the Imperial questions of burden, constraint, failure, and transition.

clues.title: The Reedwater receipt entered beside the Imperial seal
clues.description: The Emperor requires the first field acknowledgments, petitions, burden extracts, and autumn witness summons to return to the throne’s register. Reedwater’s standing therefore becomes part of implementation, not a courtesy exhausted by testimony.
clues.discovery: Available if the presentation names how provincial witnesses receive, challenge, and review the adopted Mandate.
